title: Solutions and Solubility
seo_title: Grade 5 Science: Solutions and Solubility Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Solutions are homogeneous mixtures: dissolving, solubility of solids, liquids and gases, concentration and pH, and separating solutions by evaporation, distillation and crystallization. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 5, Chemistry)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets (BC): solutes and solvents, dissolving, saturated solutions, and separating solutions by evaporation and distillation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A solution is a mixture that looks the same all through.
key_sub: The solute dissolves in the solvent.
body_html:
How to think about it

When sugar dissolves in water, the sugar (solute) spreads evenly through the water (solvent) to make a solution. Stirring, heating and smaller pieces make solids dissolve faster. A saturated solution cannot dissolve any more solute at that temperature.

Solutions can be separated: evaporation leaves the solid behind (salt from salt water), distillation collects the liquid, and crystallization grows crystals as water evaporates slowly.

Example

In salt water, which is the solvent?

The substance there is more of

Answer: water

Example

How can you get salt back from salt water?

Let the water go.

Answer: evaporate the water

Common mistakes

  • Thinking dissolved sugar is gone (it is still there).
  • Mixing up solute and solvent.
  • Thinking filtering can separate a solution.

items.q: What is the principle behind distillation?
c: Insoluble solid particles are too big to pass through the tiny holes in the filter paper.
The solvent changes into a gas and escapes, leaving the dissolved solid behind.
Different dyes have different solubilities in the solvent, so they travel different distances.
The liquid with the lower boiling point boils first, and its vapour is cooled and condensed.
items.e: This is how distillation works.
